newsitem.title: UK: Brother of UK's Kray twins convicted for drugs.
newsitem.headline: Brother of UK's Kray twins convicted for drugs.

text.p: The elder brother of the Kray twins, the gangsters who terrorised east London in the 1960s, was found guilty on Friday of trying to smuggle 39 million pounds ($65 million) worth of cocaine into Britain.

Charlie Kray, 70, was charged with offering to suppy two undercover police officers with five kg (11 lbs) of cocaine every fortnight for two years. He was also found guilty of actually supplying two kg (4.4 lbs).
The defence portrayed Kray as a poor and sick old man who had pretended to have access to drugs to try to make some money out of the officers.
Kray and his two accompices will be sentenced on Monday.
Charlie Kray had spent his life in the shade of his infamous younger brothers, Ronnie and Reggie Kray, who were jailed for life in 1969 for gangland murders.
Ronnie died of a heart attack last year in Broadmoor psychiatric hospital, home to many of Britain's most disturbed criminals. Reggie, 62, remains in prison.

The Kray twins' thuggery has become romanticised over the years they have been in prison. A film was made of their lives, and their defenders argue that their reign helped to keep peace in the impoverished East End of London. They say the brothers only ever attacked other villains.
Charlie Kray's friends and relatives said they would appeal against his conviction.

"Charlie would never even supply a cigarette. We have just got to appeal. It is just outrageous. He is a victim of his surname and circumstances with no real evidence," his former girlfriend told reporters.
